title: Per-queue worker concurrency (WORKER_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY)
description:
Every queue an instance works on gets the same `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` goroutines. That does not fit queues whose handlers call a rate-limited service (we want `reports` one at a time) next to queues that should go wide.

- New `WORKER_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY`, a comma-separated list of `queue=n` entries such as `emails=2,reports=1`, overrides `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` for the queues it names; the others keep the default. With `WORKER_CONCURRENCY=0` only the named queues get workers.
- Validated at startup with the other settings: each queue must be one of `WORKER_QUEUES`, each value an integer from 1 to 256 (the same bound as `WORKER_CONCURRENCY`), each queue listed once, and each entry must look like `queue=n`.
- `worker.Options.QueueConcurrency` carries the overrides; `NewPool` rejects an override for a queue the pool does not work on or a value below 1, and keeps its own copy of the map. `Start` launches the right number of goroutines per queue (lease owner names stay `<ID>/<queue>/<n>`) and logs the per-queue counts.
- New gauge `jobqueue_workers{queue}`: the goroutines started for each queue.
- `cmd/jobqueue` passes the setting through; README documents it.

Tests: config parsing and every error, `NewPool` validation, and a pool with three queues where blocking handlers show how many goroutines each queue runs at once, plus the gauge.
